transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-11-12 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Nora Alvarez (HelioFleet Platform Eng), Benji Osei (HelioFleet SRE), Dr. Priya Rao (HelioFleet CTO)

Auto Summary (auto-generated - may be imperfect):
Redwood and HelioFleet discussed intermittent tail latency after the node kernel/driver patch last week, a suspected MTU/path-MTU issue on the VPC peering links, BGP route flaps causing delayed route convergence to the private cluster, and degraded KV cache hit rates on warmups. Action items include packet captures, firewall rule confirmations, a canary kernel upgrade window, and Redwood sharing a rollback playbook and patched release notes.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, thanks everyone for joining. I'll kick us off — this is the weekly pilot sync for HelioFleet. We've got the notes from last week pulled in, Arjun's got the logs up, Nora and Benji from your side. How's the morning over there?
[00:12] Nora Alvarez: Morning, yeah — we saw another sporadic latency spike yesterday around 11:30 my time, about a 300 to 400 millisecond tail on some 512 token requests. Not consistent but enough to trigger our alerting.
[00:26] Benji Osei: Yeah and I want to point out we had two BGP withdraws from the transit path, might be related. We're still pinning down whether it's the peering fabric or the host NIC driver after the kernel bump.
[00:40] Arjun Patel: Right, we've been correlating traces. On our side p99 looked fine for most paths except when the route flap coincided with a cold KV cache miss. The combination seems multiplicative — cache miss + route reconvergence equals big tail.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Hmm. Do you have the example request IDs? If you send a couple Arjun can pull the trace and the KV cache hit ratio for that window.
[01:15] Benji Osei: I'll drop three in the chat after the call.
[01:20] Nora Alvarez: Quick context — we moved to MTU 9000 on the cluster and some of the peering devices were sync'd after the kernel upgrade. We suspect fragmentation behavior changed.
[01:33] Arjun Patel: Yep fragmentation behaviors can definitely surface after kernel/driver updates. Also eBPF offloads and our service mesh encapsulation interact with path MTU in odd ways. We'll want PCAPs across the hop.
[01:45] Dr. Priya Rao: Sorry to interrupt — from a business perspective we need this to be stable for the pilot demo next month. Can you give us a clear canary plan and signal gates?
[01:55] Maya Chen: Absolutely — that's the anchor. We'll outline canary windows, rollback triggers (packet loss > 1% or p99 increase > 150 ms for three consecutive 5-minute buckets), and automatic fallback to hosted for critical endpoints.
[02:10] Benji Osei: About fallback — what's the latency delta when you fallback to Redwood hosted? In pre-tests we saw an extra 30–50ms but that's acceptable compared to 300ms tails.
[02:22] Arjun Patel: On average hosted adds ~35ms median, but the variance is small; and we can route selectively by route/tag so only the most latency-sensitive traffic is directed to hosted as short-term mitigation.
[02:35] Nora Alvarez: Ok that helps. On the technical side we captured kernel logs around the time of the flaps; the NIC reported a firmware reset per host — could be the 10.2.1 driver.
[02:48] Arjun Patel: We flagged the 10.2.1 driver as a potential regression in our internal lab. We have a patched runtime that avoids a specific offload path. We can schedule a canary kernel upgrade to test the patch on a small subset of nodes.
[03:05] Dr. Priya Rao: What's the rollback story if the canary shows regression?
[03:12] Maya Chen: Rollback is twofold: immediate traffic steering to hosted and a node-level kernel rollback via your standard image — we will provide the rollback playbook steps and a script to mark nodes out of service before reimaging.
[03:25] Benji Osei: Sounds good. A practical ask — can Redwood own the initial packet capture collection? We can give a temporary collector role but we worry about exposure.
[03:36] Arjun Patel: We can provide a packet-capture checklist and a small capture tool that runs for a bounded window and strips payloads. That keeps things minimal. We'll send that checklist by tomorrow.
[03:50] Nora Alvarez: Please remove payloads — compliance requires. Also include guidance for capturing MTU blackhole patterns and TCP MSS clamping.
[04:02] Maya Chen: Noted.
[04:06] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[04:10] Arjun Patel: Another data point — we saw KV cache warmup times were worse after the kernel bump. The cache warmup is sensitive to packet reordering and small tail latencies, which pushes more upstream requests and creates cascading misses.
[04:24] Benji Osei: Does Redwood have recommendations for pre-warming? We've tried synthetic prefix playback but haven't matched production shape.
[04:33] Arjun Patel: Two approaches: 1) intelligent prefix warming from the last week of traffic sampled at 1% — we can generate a warmup workload that matches your token length distribution; 2) maintain a small hot shard of workers pinned with higher memory and preloaded KV state for the first 60s of a traffic burst. Both have tradeoffs (cost vs latency).
[04:58] Nora Alvarez: Hot shard idea is intriguing — but would that affect autoscaler decisions? We already saw an autoscaler misfire last week that spun down a warm node.
[05:08] Arjun Patel: You can exclude hot-shard nodes from the autoscaler by tag, or use a soft-min pool. We'll add the config snippet to the docs.
[05:18] Maya Chen: On observability, we noticed gaps in per-route tracing logs when the BGP withdraw happened. Benji, are you able to export the route-change window logs to us?
[05:30] Benji Osei: Yes, I'll attach the route-change logs and the control-plane snapshots. Expect those in the CRM ticket by EOD.
[05:40] Dr. Priya Rao: One security question — during fallback to hosted, how is customer data protected? We need KMS integration details and audit logs.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Good question. Fallback to hosted uses your tenant in our hosted control plane. Data in flight is TLS; at-rest is encrypted with per-customer keys. We support KMS integrations — we can share SOC2 section and architecture diagram. We'll attach the security pack.
[06:10] Nora Alvarez: Please include tokens and retention periods — compliance wants specifics.
[06:16] Maya Chen: We'll include that.
[06:20] Arjun Patel: Small note on routing policy — currently you're using egress NAT through a shared transit. If you can carve a dedicated path for the private pilot VPC with stable BGP next-hops we reduce convergence time.
[06:33] Benji Osei: We'll evaluate with our network team but it's extra ops. Could we implement BGP dampening or service mesh retries instead?
[06:44] Arjun Patel: BGP dampening helps but can mask flaps; better to reduce underlying flaps. Service mesh retries can hide the symptom but add retry amplification. We recommend fixing the underlying NIC/driver first and using mesh-level retries as a short-term mitigation.
[07:01] Maya Chen: OK, so tangible plan: 1) collect PCAPs + kernel logs for two representative incidents; 2) Redwood sends checklist and capture tool; 3) schedule canary kernel upgrade on a small subset with rollback playbook; 4) run a perf benchmark with prefix warmup and share spreadsheet. Does that align?
[07:18] Dr. Priya Rao: Yes, and please define success criteria — otherwise we keep chasing symptoms.
[07:24] Maya Chen: Success criteria proposed: p99 latency <= 120ms and no BGP withdraws impacting >5% of nodes during canary; KV cache hit ratio improves by >=8% after warmup. We can iterate those with you.
[07:39] Nora Alvarez: We'll chew on those numbers and confirm by EOD tomorrow.
[07:44] Speaker 2: (muted)
[07:48] Benji Osei: Quick ops question — Arjun, when you said the patched runtime avoids an offload path, does that carry CPU overhead? We can't accept a big CPU bump.
[07:58] Arjun Patel: The patch disables a small NIC offload (checksum offload path) in the runtime for affected packet shapes; it adds roughly 4–6% CPU for affected tokens in our microbenchmarks but reduces  tail events in the regression scenario. We can limit the patch to canary nodes.
[08:18] Maya Chen: Also we can do a staged config: enable patch only for nodes that see the problematic NIC driver version.
[08:26] Nora Alvarez: Perfect. On timing — when can Redwood run the canary? We have a maintenance window Friday 02:00–06:00 UTC.
[08:35] Maya Chen: We propose 2025-11-19 02:00 UTC for canary step 1; that gives us time to collect pcaps and validate the patch. We'll put a detailed runbook with prechecks.
[08:48] Benji Osei: We want a pre-check list — health checks, baseline p99, control plane snapshot.
[08:56] Arjun Patel: We'll include pre/post runbook and automated verification scripts.
[09:02] Speaker 3: (background noise)
[09:06] Maya Chen: Anything else on the networking piece?
[09:09] Nora Alvarez: One more — what's Redwood asking for in terms of firewall egress? We need explicit ports, IPs.
[09:16] Arjun Patel: We'll share a minimal IP list and ranges, plus guidance for ephemeral control plane endpoints and certificate pinning notes.
[09:24] Maya Chen: For telemetry, we'll add a short dashboard in the console that highlights p99, kv-hit-rate, route-change counts for the pilot cluster.
[09:33] Dr. Priya Rao: That'll help exec review.
[09:36] Maya Chen: Great. Last blocker — do you need us to run a synthetic traffic replay to stress the warmup?
[09:44] Nora Alvarez: Yes please, but we need the generator to match our token distribution and at-most-once semantics. We've seen synthetic generators create unrealistic concurrency.
[09:53] Arjun Patel: We have a traffic-replay harness that samples your historical traces at 0.5% and scales to your peak rate; we'll parameterize concurrency and token lengths. We can run it during the canary window in a gray fashion (non-prod endpoint) first.
[10:08] Benji Osei: Good. Please ensure we can throttle it quickly.
[10:12] Arjun Patel: Absolutely.
[10:15] Maya Chen: Wrap-up time — I'll summarize next steps in the CRM ticket. Benji, Nora, any last asks?
[10:22] Nora Alvarez: Just one ask — include exact retention for any captures and ensure auto-delete after 7 days unless we opt-in.
[10:29] Maya Chen: Will do.
[10:31] Benji Osei: That's all from me.
[10:33] Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks, team.
[10:35] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the checklist, patched notes, and schedule the canary.
